parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal, entry, facility or custody rule is documented; the state instead assesses a visitor against documents as issued, with no gender-recognition route, so a mismatch surfaces at checkpoints and hotels. Around that gap sit the factors that matter: a public-morals statute penalising public same-sex affection (6 months–2 years, harsher than comparable offences), entrenched societal discrimination, SOGI framed as 'imported', no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, no functioning trans civil society, and a documented domestic record of arrests on false accusations of same-sex intercourse together with police mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people, in a context of impunity for security-force violence. Trans-specific violence data is absent, not exculpatory. This resolves to High Risk: outing carries real prospects of humiliation, extortion, arrest-adjacent policing and violence with no realistic remedy, but not a documented trans-specific carceral or lethal pipeline.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; officials assess the visitor against documents as issued, so a marker/presentation mismatch surfaces at the border and in routine checks.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented trans-specific entry rule, denial practice, or X-marker recognition.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into secondary questioning and, given the police record, into discretionary detention; foreign documents are not documented as accepted at face value.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A local civil-society organisation documents arrests prompted by false accusations of same-sex intercourse and mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement; impunity for security-force violence is the only custody context available.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No trans-specific custody protocol, consular-access guarantee, or oversight body shown to operate.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor drawn into any investigation would be held under general (harsh, impunity-affected) conditions with no documented identity-congruent placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access, bathroom, ward-placement or segregation rule aimed at trans people, and no gender-recognition route to align any paperwork.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facilities are governed by unstated practice; hospital or shelter admission would proceed on birth-sex paperwork with no documented remedy.

care_services.exposure: No anti-discrimination law in health; conversion practices not banned; discrimination in healthcare documented; HIV status used to stigmatise. Trans-specific care rules unstated.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can itself out the visitor to staff with no documented recourse if refused or humiliated.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 85 punishes public same-sex affection as an attack on public morals (6 months–2 years or fine), heavier than other morals offences; SOGI publicly framed as 'imported' and contrary to local values; police mistreatment documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Private same-sex conduct between consenting adults is legal; 2012 recorded no arrests under the provisions (stale).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: A trans visitor whose relationship reads as same-sex under birth-sex status is exposed to the morals article, and the statute supplies social licence for police hostility toward gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penalties rise to 2–5 years where a child is a participant; that provision concerns sexual conduct, not guardianship. Discrimination in education documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor faces heightened official suspicion around an outed trans identity, with no documented safeguarding or service pathway.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Entrenched societal discrimination and forced concealment documented; LGBTQ people keep identities hidden; no anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute; complaints to police carry documented mistreatment risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. The 2023 'no reports of violence' figure is undetermined between absence and non-reporting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims have no realistic route to remedy, so predation and extortion against a visibly trans foreigner would go unaddressed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal gender recognition, no non-discrimination protections, no known LGBTQ rights organisations; data-protection sensitive-data clause names sexual orientation only, not gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. Two UPR recommendations and endorsement of the UN joint statement are diplomatic signals without operative effect shown.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No working recourse exists at any stage from border desk to police station to clinic.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor documents trans-specific police extortion, document confiscation and overnight cells. This dossier lacks trans-specific enforcement evidence but adds a morals statute reaching same-sex public affection and documented police torture of LGBTQ people, so it sits somewhat above that anchor but in the same broad tier.

That anchor shows a documented, routine trans-visitor stop-and-detain pattern with fines and no effective remedy. Here no trans-specific stop pattern is documented, but the police-abuse record plus statutory morals offence and total absence of recourse produce comparable severity with wider uncertainty.

That anchor limits harm to border secondary screening, refused admission and return transport, with written decisions and an appeal desk. This dossier shows no such procedural safeguards and adds police mistreatment, so it rates materially lower.

That anchor features trained border officers, tribunal appeals and compensation for unlawful detention. None of that machinery is documented here; the only oversight is external review recommendations with no shown effect, so this case is far below.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a single national system with no subnational variation. Private conduct is lawful, but the only visible legal lever — Article 85's morals offence against public same-sex affection — reaches a trans visitor read as same-sex under birth-sex documents and carries penalties heavier than comparable offences. Documents cannot be aligned (no gender recognition), so discovery is plausible at borders, hotels and checkpoints, and the documented response to LGBTQ people is concealment, discrimination, false-accusation arrests and police mistreatment amid general impunity. With no anti-discrimination law, no trans civil society and no working remedy, the ordinary frictions of an outing escalate rather than resolve. Harm stops short of a documented trans-specific carceral or lethal pathway, which keeps this out of the Severe band, but the absence of any documented protection places it firmly in High Risk.
